claims.text: High-temperature oxidation of group IV–V RMPEAs induces a graded hierarchy of microstructural heterogeneities.
The oxidation-induced heterogeneities include nanoscale interstitial complexes and tertiary phases near the oxide-adjacent region.
The hierarchical heterogeneities act as barriers to oxygen diffusion.
The hierarchical heterogeneities act as barriers to crack propagation.
Oxidation-induced hierarchical heterogeneities enhance oxidation resistance.
Oxidation-induced hierarchical heterogeneities maintain material integrity.
Oxygen ingress triggers localized phase changes in group IV–V RMPEAs.
The localized phase changes form a graded microstructural barrier.
Oxidation-induced heterogeneities substantially increase local hardness.
The graded barrier impedes continued oxygen diffusion.
The graded barrier reduces the oxidation rate.
The graded barrier delays crack initiation relative to alloys not exposed to oxygen.
Oxidized group IV–V RMPEAs exhibit a hardness gradient extending from oxide-adjacent metal toward the surface oxide.
Oxidized samples will have a slower effective oxygen diffusion rate than samples maintained in an inert atmosphere.
The inert-atmosphere baseline will exhibit minimal microstructural heterogeneity.
The inert-atmosphere baseline will exhibit a lower hardness gradient than the oxidized material.
The proposed governing behavior applies to group IV–V RMPEAs under sustained oxidation up to approximately 1200°C.
In tailored Y- and Hf-containing NiCoCrAl-type MPEAs, lattice distortion can suppress sustained diffusion by increasing vacancy formation energy and aluminum migration barriers.
The behavior under fluctuating oxygen partial pressures or at temperatures significantly above 1200°C has not been established.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a lower oxygen diffusion rate in oxidized samples than in an inert-atmosphere control. Because the inert control has no comparable oxygen ingress, its measured oxygen profile should be negligible; this does not provide a coherent baseline for claiming that oxidation reduced oxygen diffusion. A matched oxidizing baseline alloy or intrinsic tracer-diffusivity comparison would be needed.

The mechanism claims a reduced oxidation rate relative to alloys not exposed to oxygen, while the baseline is maintained in inert atmosphere and therefore should undergo essentially no oxidation. Oxidation resistance cannot be established from oxidation-rate comparison with that baseline.
